title: Scheduled flow suite run reported a false failure: the laptop host slept and the embedded runner lost its job lease
summary: The 19:00Z scheduled suite run started on a laptop in a 45 s battery maintenance wake. The suites run on the runner embedded in the local CLI, so when the host slept again at ~19:00:21Z, the `anchor: invitations` run stopped heartbeating and Echopoint failed it after its 30 s lease (`runner lease expired before completion`). The host slept until the lid opened at 19:22Z, so the anchor suite took 22 min instead of ~3 and reported 22/23. The flow passed twice on rerun; no product defect. The routine now runs suites through `run_suites.sh`, which holds a sleep assertion, reruns lease-expired flows once and prints the host sleep log, and the flow-suite-testing skill names host interruption as a diagnosis class.

impact.text: One false red flow in the anchor suite and a 22 min suite run. Dev only, no customer impact. Without the rule, the false failure could have opened a known-bugs flow or a product postmortem.

trigger: The host went back to sleep at ~19:00:21Z, 45 s after the maintenance wake that started the scheduled run.
detection: The routine saw the anchor suite still running after 22 min with `INVALID_JOB_TOKEN` and `RUNNER_JOB_COMPLETION_REJECTED` in the CLI log, then matched the gap to `pmset -g log`. A similar 2026-10-15 heartbeat reset was retried with no record, so the first occurrence was missed.
resolution: A sleep assertion (`caffeinate`) was attached to the running suite, and the interrupted flow was rerun twice, green. `run_suites.sh` now does both by default.

events.label: Earlier heartbeat reset retried, not recorded
events.detail: Run log 2026-10-15T17:08Z: one transient runner heartbeat reset, retried.

Echopoint fails the run: lease expired

Sleep assertion attached to the running suite
Interrupted flow green twice on rerun

whys.problem: The scheduled suite run reported `anchor: invitations` as failed, but the product was correct

because.text: Echopoint failed the execution because its runner stopped heartbeating for longer than the 30 s lease
because.evidence: Execution `01a14b3c-6f52-…` error `runner lease expired before completion`; `defaultRunnerLeaseTTL = 30 * time.Second`

because.text: The runner was the one embedded in the local CLI, and the host went to sleep mid-run
because.evidence: `flows run` launches `(ephemeral)`; `pmset -g log` DarkWake 18:59:36Z for 45 s, then Sleep until 19:22:00Z lid wake

because.text: The scheduler starts the routine in a short battery maintenance wake, and nothing in the run held the host awake
because.evidence: `DarkWake ... rtc/Maintenance Using BATT ... 45 secs`; suite command had no `caffeinate`

because.text: The suite run procedure had no sleep guard, though it runs for minutes on a host that sleeps on its own
Scheduled suites run on a laptop runner by design; the Cloud runner would not depend on the host
because.evidence: Run notes: `echopoint flows run` executes on the CLI's embedded runner

because.text: Scheduled suite execution is placed on a host whose power state the routine does not control
The false failure looked like a product failure and the first occurrence went unrecorded
because.evidence: CLI shows only `✗ Flow ...: error` with a 409; 2026-10-15 run log: heartbeat reset retried, no ledger row

because.text: The routine had no rule that separates host interruption from product or platform failure
Diagnosis guidance listed product, setup, provider and quota causes, but not a runner host that sleeps or drops its network

contributing: The laptop was on battery (39%), where macOS sleeps with the lid closed whatever assertions apps hold.

well: Echopoint failed the orphaned run after 30 s with a clear error message instead of leaving it running.
The CLI moved on to the next flow after the rejection, so the rest of the suite still ran.
wrong: The 2026-10-15 occurrence was retried with no record, so the cause stayed unknown for two days.
lucky: The user opened the lid at 19:22Z; otherwise the suite could have run for hours and overlapped a post-deploy gate (409 FLOW_TREE_CONFLICT).
The sleep hit a flow that does not own long-lived data; an interrupted run before its `always` cleanup could leave a throwaway org behind.

actions.what: Run suites through `run_suites.sh`: `caffeinate -ims`, rerun lease-expired flows once, print the host sleep log for the run window
Name host interruption (lease-expired, job-token rejection) as a diagnosis class in the flow-suite-testing skill
Decide where scheduled suites run: an always-on host (or AC power), or Cloud launches within the CI org daily budget

messaging.internal: Suite run 2026-10-17T19:00Z: `anchor: invitations` false red because the laptop slept mid-run (lease expired). Rerun green twice. Suites now run under a sleep guard with an automatic rerun of host-interrupted flows.
